scope_note: Daily edition from matching Thursday /new listings: 107 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 51 cs.RO rows, 154 deduplicated papers, and 124 ROI papers. Tier A cards are conservative abstract-only autopsies from the repository parser output; no figure, table, full-text, code, or dataset-release claims are asserted.
executive_thesis: The August 27 batch is about turning broad model capability into accountable control variables. VLA and WAM papers ask which geometric, temporal, tactile, retrieval, or embodiment interface actually changes an action. Mapping and 3D reconstruction papers make pose, calibration, weather, water, and LiDAR supervision part of the release contract rather than background assumptions. Driving and multi-robot papers push risk evidence into trajectories before a planner commits, while VLM papers replace fluent answers with point, rubric, benchmark, and retrieval evidence. APRL's strongest move is to own evaluation suites where a policy, map, world model, or visual reasoner must expose the evidence that grants or revokes permission to act.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Robot foundation models are becoming interface contracts
decision_cards.body: GaussVLA, V-Link, StreamPI, Zero-WAM, 4DGS-WAM, and ConfAL-WM all ask which spatial, temporal, or confidence interface lets a robot trust a large model output.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Manipulation adaptation is moving into execution time
decision_cards.body: RA-VLA, TacForcing, VISTA, LM-X, MA-VLA, and unified action geometry papers separate retrieval, contact, tactile feedback, progress, uncertainty, and embodiment as control variables.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Autonomy evidence must arrive before commitment
decision_cards.body: CoRE, TAU-Agent, SkyDrive, DESCENT, Gating Before Commitment, game-structure measurement, and trust-aware rollout planning treat risk as a trajectory signal rather than a final label.

papers.title: GaussVLA: Geometry-Aware Spatial Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.fit: VLA spatial reasoning - 3D Gaussian tokens - action grounding
papers.status_quo: VLA policies often pass flat 2D patch tokens into an action head and hope depth or semantics are recovered implicitly.
papers.friction: The abstract argues that dense monocular depth gives scalar values but not structured surface orientation, confidence, or compact geometry for action prediction.
papers.hidden_premise: A robot action should be conditioned on a compressed geometric object that carries uncertainty and salient spatial structure, not only image patches.
papers.conceptual_move: Reframe VLA perception as Gaussian-token spatial reasoning plus depth-aware chain-of-thought for action selection.
papers.mechanism: The abstract names a Gaussian Spatial Tokenizer and depth-aware reasoning module as the route from frozen semantic/depth features to compact 3D evidence.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies flat 2D patch tokens as lacking intrinsic geometric structure for VLA action prediction.
It proposes compact 3D Gaussian tokens that pool geometrically salient regions with learned queries.
APRL should test whether Gaussian-token reasoning changes manipulation failures under viewpoint and depth-confidence shifts.

papers.falsification: If Gaussian tokens improve language or perception probes but do not change action selection under spatial stress, the interface is not yet control-relevant.
papers.adversarial: Use object pose swaps, depth noise, partial occlusion, and distractor geometry to separate real spatial reasoning from benchmark-specific token regularization.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask which geometric evidence enters the action head and when it changes the motor command.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA manipulation and mobile manipulation; weaker for tasks where explicit geometry is already supplied by a trusted state estimator.

papers.title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization
papers.fit: world-action modeling - human video context - task generalization
papers.status_quo: Cross-task robot generalization is usually handled through parameter updates, large robot datasets, or text task descriptions.
papers.friction: The abstract says language alone is a weak task specification for manipulation because it omits rich visual evolution of the intended task.
papers.hidden_premise: Human videos can act as executable task context only if the model preserves which state changes matter for the robot, not only the appearance sequence.
papers.conceptual_move: Bring in-context learning to robot manipulation by using human video as the task specification for a world-action model.
papers.mechanism: The abstract frames human-video context as a way to specify open-ended manipulation tasks without parameter updates.

evidence.claim: The paper names zero-shot cross-task generalization as a central robot learning challenge.
It argues that human video gives richer cues about intended task evolution than language.
APRL should benchmark which human-video cues transfer to robot actions and which become misleading appearance priors.

papers.falsification: If human-video context helps only when embodiment, viewpoint, and object dynamics match the robot setup, the method is not open-ended generalization.
papers.adversarial: Vary embodiment, camera viewpoint, hand-object contact, and irrelevant human motion while measuring robot action deviation and task success.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat demonstrations as task-specification evidence, then test which parts survive the human-to-robot boundary.
papers.transfer_boundary: Useful for open-ended manipulation; less direct for low-level control where human video lacks actuator-relevant timing.

papers.title: 4DGS-WAM: Bridging Past and Future with an Object-Centric World Action Model based on 4D Gaussian Splatting
papers.fit: 4D Gaussian world-action model - object-centric dynamics - future prediction
papers.status_quo: Many WAMs operate on 2D visual streams that can repeatedly process redundant background and hide object-level spatial dynamics.
papers.friction: The abstract says 2D visual WAMs lack explicit spatial structure for individual objects, while point clouds are hard to align and accumulate across views.
papers.hidden_premise: A control-useful world model should separate dynamic objects from static background so future actor actions can be evaluated geometrically.
papers.conceptual_move: Use 4D Gaussian Splatting as the object-centric state substrate for bridging past observations and predicted futures.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes modeling dynamic objects and static background separately, with policy-predicted actor actions and world-model transformations.

evidence.claim: The paper contrasts 2D WAMs with explicit 4D Gaussian representations for object and background structure.
It targets future prediction through object transformations rather than only whole-frame visual quality.
APRL should ask whether 4DGS state reduces action-faithfulness error under object motion and occlusion.

papers.falsification: If object-centric 4DGS improves rendering but not action-conditioned state prediction, the representation is not yet a robot world model.
papers.adversarial: Test moving-object swaps, static-background changes, occlusions, and contact transitions while measuring future object pose and policy decisions.
papers.thinking_tool: Separate what can move, what should stay fixed, and what action is allowed to transform.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for object-centric manipulation and driving scenes; weaker for texture-only video generation.

papers.title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation
papers.fit: VLA test-time adaptation - retrieval - executable actions
papers.status_quo: In-context imitation often assumes that retrieving similar demonstrations is enough to adapt a VLA at test time.
papers.friction: The abstract argues that superficial retrieval and behavioral inertia can prevent expert context from becoming executable action.
papers.hidden_premise: A retrieved context is useful only if it overcomes pretrained policy inertia at the moment of action generation.
papers.conceptual_move: Treat retrieval as an adaptation operator whose success must be measured through changed executable behavior, not context similarity.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a retrieval-augmented VLA framework designed to translate expert context into actions under novel task distributions.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies brittleness under novel task distributions as a VLA limitation.
It names superficial retrieval and behavioral inertia as adaptation bottlenecks.
APRL should test when retrieved examples actually alter action choice before terminal success changes.

papers.falsification: If retrieval improves nearest-neighbor similarity but the action distribution stays anchored to pretrained priors, the adaptation is cosmetic.
papers.adversarial: Use visually similar demonstrations with different contact order, object affordance, or goal constraint to expose false retrieval authority.
papers.thinking_tool: Evaluate retrieval by the action it changes, not the example it returns.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA adaptation; weaker for policies with explicit symbolic task planners that already separate retrieval from control.

papers.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
papers.fit: contact-rich manipulation - tactile feedback - streaming action generation
papers.status_quo: Chunk-based VLA policies often predict an action segment from pre-execution observations and handle fast contact changes with separate controllers.
papers.friction: The abstract says contact states can evolve within an action horizon, making pre-chunk tactile conditioning stale during execution.
papers.hidden_premise: A manipulation policy must refresh contact evidence while the action is unfolding, not only before the chunk starts.
papers.conceptual_move: Make tactile feedback part of streaming action generation instead of delegating it to a separate reactive controller.
papers.mechanism: The abstract frames TacForcing as incorporating execution-time tactile feedback inside the action-generation process.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies stale tactile conditioning as a failure mode for chunk-based VLA policies.
It proposes streaming action generation that uses tactile feedback during execution.
APRL should evaluate whether tactile refresh changes recovery timing and contact stability.

papers.falsification: If streaming tactile feedback does not improve failures with slipping, contact transitions, or occlusion, the added channel is not carrying the decisive state.
papers.adversarial: Sweep slip, compliance, occlusion, and object material while comparing chunk-only, reactive-controller, and streaming-action policies.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat contact as a state that expires inside the action horizon.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for contact-rich manipulation; weaker for free-space reaching with little tactile ambiguity.

papers.title: PIVOT: A Multi-Trajectory Dataset and Testbed for Pose, Intrinsics, and Novel Viewpoint Evaluation in Real-World 3D Reconstruction
papers.fit: 3D reconstruction evaluation - pose and intrinsics - robot viewpoint shift
papers.status_quo: NeRF and 3DGS methods are often evaluated with reconstruction-friendly trajectories, optimized camera poses, and held-out views similar to training paths.
papers.friction: The abstract argues these assumptions can obscure performance when robots use measured poses, reusable calibration, and structurally different camera paths.
papers.hidden_premise: Robot-usable reconstruction should be tested under camera and trajectory conditions that match deployment, not only clean novel-view synthesis settings.
papers.conceptual_move: Move 3D reconstruction evaluation from appearance quality to pose, intrinsics, and trajectory robustness.
papers.mechanism: The abstract introduces a multi-trajectory testbed oriented around pose, intrinsics, and novel viewpoint evaluation.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies reconstruction-friendly trajectories and optimized camera assumptions as benchmark weaknesses.
It introduces PIVOT for measured poses, reusable camera calibration, and structurally different camera paths.
APRL should grade map representations by robot camera trajectories and calibration stress.

papers.falsification: If PIVOT rankings still track ordinary clean novel-view benchmarks, the new protocol may not expose a deployment-relevant failure.
papers.adversarial: Use robot-like viewpoint shifts, calibration reuse, pose noise, and held-out trajectories unlike training paths.
papers.thinking_tool: A reconstruction benchmark should attack the camera assumptions a robot cannot guarantee.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for mapping and robot scene assets; less direct for artistic 3D generation where camera calibration is not a deployment contract.

papers.title: SUPER ODOMETRY 2.0: Resilient Odometry via Hierarchical Adaptation
papers.fit: resilient odometry - sensor degradation - hierarchical adaptation
papers.status_quo: Odometry systems often rely on a fixed fusion recipe that assumes sensors degrade within expected environmental limits.
papers.friction: The abstract names smoke, sandstorms, snow, and low-light conditions as severe degradations that threaten robot safety and functionality.
papers.hidden_premise: A field odometry stack should adapt at multiple levels before state estimation becomes unrecoverable.
papers.conceptual_move: Define resilient odometry as hierarchical adaptation across feature selection, sensing, fusion, and higher-level recovery.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a sensor fusion framework that dynamically adapts to varying levels of environmental degradation.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies severe sensory degradation as a failure mode for existing odometry systems.
It proposes hierarchical modules for adaptability under changing environmental conditions.
APRL should connect odometry confidence to downstream navigation recovery, not only trajectory error.

papers.falsification: If adaptation lowers trajectory error but does not improve mission recovery or failure prediction under degradation, the hierarchy is incomplete.
papers.adversarial: Test low light, smoke, dust, snow, feature scarcity, and dynamic-object interference while measuring localization drift and recovery action.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat odometry as a resilience system with staged fallbacks, not a single estimator.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for field robots and autonomous navigation; weaker for static indoor datasets with mild sensor change.

papers.title: Gating Before Commitment: Anticipating Intent Divergence to Prevent Post-Interaction Decision Failures in Autonomous Driving
papers.fit: driving interaction risk - intent divergence - pre-commitment gating
papers.status_quo: Autonomous driving planners often treat intent interpretation as upstream context and commit to a maneuver once a trajectory is selected.
papers.friction: The abstract argues that intent misinterpretation during vehicle interactions causes recurring planning failures.
papers.hidden_premise: A planner needs a pre-commitment gate that can revoke a maneuver when intent and geometry start to diverge.
papers.conceptual_move: Move interaction understanding into a decision layer that gates the planned maneuver before commitment.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a language-guided intent module that computes smoothed intent-geometry divergence upstream of a corridor envelope.

evidence.claim: The paper names intent misinterpretation as a source of post-interaction planning failures.
It frames divergence scoring as a gate before the maneuver is committed.
APRL should evaluate whether early divergence signals create recoverable windows before constraint violation.

papers.falsification: If the gate fires only after a recoverable trajectory is gone, it is an explanation layer rather than a safety layer.
papers.adversarial: Replay ambiguous negotiation, off-road departure, late yielding, and adversarial descriptor cases while measuring warning lead time and plan repair.
papers.thinking_tool: Safety evidence has to arrive before commitment, not after failure attribution.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for interactive driving and multi-robot navigation; weaker for isolated single-agent planning without intent coupling.

synthesis.title: VLA/WAM papers are naming the state that grants action authority
synthesis.facts: The abstracts focus on 3D Gaussian tokens, recovered visual representations, streaming temporal units, human-video context, object-centric 4D state, and confidence-guided active learning.
synthesis.inference: The shared decision is to expose which intermediate state is allowed to change a robot action under distribution shift.

synthesis.title: Contact and embodiment are becoming online variables
synthesis.links: RA-VLA - TacForcing - VISTA - LM-X - MA-VLA - UCAG-P
synthesis.facts: The batch separates retrieval authority, execution-time tactile feedback, visual contact deformation, progress/event/uncertainty prediction, arm assignment, and camera-centric action geometry.
synthesis.inference: APRL should evaluate adaptation by when the interface changes the action, not by a final few-shot success score alone.

synthesis.title: Risk evidence is moving upstream of planner commitment
synthesis.links: CoRE - TAU-Agent - SkyDrive - DESCENT - Gating Before Commitment - Trust-aware Rollout Planning
synthesis.facts: The abstracts use temporal/entity risk evidence, retrieval-selected anomaly evidence, aerial adaptation, topology-constrained forecasting, intent divergence, and trust monitors.
synthesis.inference: A safety benchmark should measure warning lead time and repair windows before the policy crosses the constraint boundary.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: August 24-26 already emphasized action authorization, evidence routing, WAM action faithfulness, and physically executable scene assets.
frontier_memory.body: August 27 strengthens the same axis with geometry-aware VLA tokens, object-centric 4D WAMs, tactile streaming, retrieval adaptation, and pre-commitment driving gates.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent reports had geometry and WAM as adjacent streams.
frontier_memory.body: Today merges them directly: GaussVLA and 4DGS-WAM make 3D Gaussian structure part of the action interface rather than only a scene representation.

frontier_memory.label: Commoditizing
frontier_memory.history: Tokenizer, pruning, diffusion, and adapter variants continue to appear across daily batches.
frontier_memory.body: The crowded implementation axis is less valuable than measured evidence preservation: which token, adapter, retrieval, or verifier prevents a wrong action.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: The repo still lacks a single benchmark that joins VLA geometry, tactile feedback, odometry degradation, and driving interaction risk.
frontier_memory.body: APRL can own a cross-task permission-to-act suite where wrong geometry, stale contact, drifting localization, and late intent evidence are evaluated with the same recovery logic.

strategy.title: Permission-to-act interface suite
strategy.thesis: Evaluate whether geometry tokens, retrieved examples, tactile streams, temporal memory, and uncertainty signals actually change robot actions under stress.
strategy.one_week: Build paired manipulation cases where only geometry confidence, retrieved context, tactile event, temporal history, or embodiment mapping is corrupted.
strategy.four_week: Compare V-Link, GaussVLA-style geometry, RA-VLA retrieval, TacForcing-style tactile refresh, StreamPI temporal modeling, and UCAG-style action geometry proxies.
strategy.success: The suite predicts action changes and failure onset earlier than terminal success or average task score.
strategy.stop: If all interface variables produce the same ranking as ordinary task difficulty, split the work into geometry and contact subtracks.
strategy.asset: Stress episodes, interface-corruption labels, action-change traces, contact and geometry confidence logs, recovery-window annotations, and protocol templates.

strategy.title: Robot-usable mapping degradation benchmark
strategy.thesis: Turn pose, intrinsics, underwater turbidity, LiDAR annotation, odometry degradation, and orchard graph navigation into one mapping validity contract.
strategy.one_week: Assemble ten mapping episodes with trajectory shift, calibration perturbation, turbidity or low-light degradation, and downstream route-following tasks.
strategy.four_week: Compare 3DGS, point-cloud, feature-field, odometry-fusion, graph-navigation, and learned-waypoint pipelines under the same robot-camera stress cases.
strategy.success: Robot task success and recovery curves reorder methods relative to clean novel-view or trajectory-error scores.
strategy.stop: If downstream tasks cannot be repeated consistently, narrow the benchmark to pose/intrinsics and odometry degradation first.
strategy.asset: Trajectory splits, calibration perturbations, degradation schedules, map-validity checks, navigation outcomes, and reproducible recovery curves.

strategy.title: Pre-commitment risk evidence board
strategy.thesis: Measure whether temporal, entity, topology, intent, and trust evidence arrives early enough to repair a driving or multi-robot plan.
strategy.one_week: Replay ambiguous vehicle interactions and multi-robot spoofing cases with annotated divergence onset, evidence source, and recoverable window.
strategy.four_week: Compare risk-evidence localization, retrieval-agent explanations, aerial adaptation, topology-constrained forecasting, intent gating, and trust-aware rollout monitors.
strategy.success: Evidence lead time predicts whether a planner can repair before corridor, collision, or assignment failure.
strategy.stop: If evidence is only explanatory after commitment, move the effort to offline failure taxonomy instead of online planning.
strategy.asset: Interaction clips, entity-risk intervals, topology constraints, intent-divergence traces, trust-monitor outputs, and repair-window metrics.
